captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a drill-press cross-slide vise constructed from dark gray and black components. It features a heavy rectangular base with mounting slots, a lower sliding stage that moves along a longitudinal dovetail rail, and an upper sliding stage with jaws that moves transversely. Two threaded drive screws, each equipped with a handwheel, control the precise sliding motions of the respective stages, while the inner faces of the jaws are lined with light-gray, textured/serrated gripping plates.
captions.instruction: Design a 3D model of a drill-press cross-slide vise in CadQuery. It should feature a sturdy rectangular base with slots, a longitudinal translation stage, a transverse jaw stage with textured gripping plates, and two rotating handwheel drive screws to control the orthogonal movements.
captions.factory: The code constructs the cross-slide vise using several distinct parts. The base is created from a box primitive with cutouts for mounting slots and a central raised guide. The longitudinal sliding stage (X-axis) and transverse jaw stage (Y-axis) are formed using combined box primitives, with thin rectangular plates added for the jaw faces. The drive screws and handwheels are modeled using cylinders and thin circular plates, which are rotated and translated into their respective positions. Prismatic joints are defined for the sliding stages, and continuous revolute joints are assigned to the handwheels.
